children.subject: a discount row's label is the promotion description verbatim and is not kept in step with the reward
children.question: if I change a promotion's reward, does the label the shopper reads change with it?
children.body: No. The label on a cart's or an order's discount row is the promotion's DESCRIPTION field verbatim -- free text an operator types once -- and nothing derives it from the reward or checks it against one. Editing the reward rewrites the money and leaves the sentence alone, in the same row: after taking one promotion from 10 percent to 20 percent and changing nothing else, the cart's expanded Discount breakdown read 'KB-LAB run12 (disposable): 10% off the cart subtotal.' beside -63.80, which is 20 percent of the 319.00 subtotal. The two came from one live read, so this is not a stale page -- it is two fields of one record that are allowed to disagree. The description is also OPTIONAL: a promotion saved with a null description renders a discount row with an EMPTY label and only an amount, so the shopper is shown money off and no reason at all (seen on a pre-existing promotion giving a flat 50.00). Since the storefront can reach the promotion's NAME nowhere -- DiscountType carries description and promotionId but no name -- the description is the ONLY human-readable thing a shopper is ever shown about a promotion, on the cart and, snapshotted, on the order forever. The shopper reads it verbatim: on an order page the Discount line expands to an internal note written by whoever created the promotion, and the same string is in the order REST payload as discounts[0].description. Treat it as a published price claim: change a reward and you must change the sentence in the same save, and never leave it empty.

why: (a) the sku synthesis and rolled-up price of the configurable order line are a separately observed side finding on the same order, unrelated to whether configuration items keep their section id

children.subject: order configuration items carry sectionId and sectionName on newer Orders module versions
children.question: does a configurable product's order line record which configuration section each chosen option answered
children.body: Read a real placed order on vcst-qa (VirtoCommerce.Orders 3.1015.0, Catalog 3.1044.0) via GET /api/order/customerOrders/{id}. Each element of the configurable line's configurationItems[] carried BOTH sectionId and sectionName alongside productId, sku, name, quantity, price, salePrice, extendedPrice, imageUrl, catalogId, categoryId, type, customText and files. The sectionIds matched exactly the section ids returned by POST /api/catalog/products/configurations/search for that product, and each chosen productId was a declared option of its own section -- so the full configuration was reconstructable from the order alone, with no ambiguity between two same-typed Product sections. Text-section customText survived byte-identical. This refines the DISPUTED entry KB-360127D0 and KB-59E4B5FC, both observed on vcptcore_stable, which state that sectionId is the one field lost when a cart configuration item crosses to the order. On this deployment it is not lost, and sectionName is additionally present. The likely explanation is a module-version difference, so the 'sectionId is lost' claim should be read as version-bound rather than general; check the Orders module version before relying on either shape.

children.subject: a configurable order line's sku is synthesized from the catalog code and its price rolls up the options
children.question: why doesn't a configurable order line's sku match the product's catalog code, and how is its price composed?
children.body: The configurable line's own sku is synthesized as 'Configuration-' + the catalog product code (order line sku 'Configuration-AGENT-TEST-CFG-013' vs catalog code 'AGENT-TEST-CFG-013'), so matching an order line sku against a catalog code fails for configurable lines; and the line's price is the rolled-up base + options (999 + 150 + 100 = 1249) with isConfigured=true and no separate lines for the option products.

why: (a) the footer-versus-console version note is an unrelated side finding next to the cookie-based session authentication

children.subject: the Vendor Portal session lives in HttpOnly cookies, so clearing local storage does not end it
children.question: How is a Vendor Portal session authenticated, and can session expiry be triggered client-side?
children.body: The Vendor Portal's API calls are authenticated by HttpOnly identity cookies, not only by the bearer data it keeps in local storage: document.cookie reads empty, corrupting the local-storage auth entry changes nothing and calls still return 200, and only clearing the cookies produces 401. No client-side change produces a 403, and /Account/Login, /account/login and /Account/AccessDenied return 404 while /connect/authorize returns 400, so session-expiry paths cannot be reached naturally.

why: (b) a later note confirms what storefront Delete member does but contradicts the remedy of deleting the account under Security > Users

children.subject: storefront Delete member only detaches the contact from the organization and leaves the account and its role
children.question: What does deleting a member from the storefront company members list actually delete?
children.body: It deletes nothing. The storefront's Delete member action calls removeMemberFromOrganization and removes the organization membership and nothing else: the row leaves the roster, but in Admin the contact still exists with its status unchanged, its security account still exists, is still Locked or Unlocked exactly as before, and STILL HOLDS the organization role it was given - an org-scoped role now assigned to an account that belongs to no organization. On the contact blade the only thing that changed is that 'Member of company(ies)' and 'Default company' are empty. Two consequences. First, removal-from-organization is invisible from the storefront, because the only representation of it is the row's absence; there is no removed state to display and no way to see a former member. Second, the email address stays taken by the surviving account, so re-inviting the same address later is not the clean slate it looks like. The storefront cannot delete the account or the contact, which means a maintainer cannot create the deleted state at all - only the detached one.

children.subject: deleting a detached member's account under Security > Users is not always possible
children.question: After a storefront member deletion, can the surviving account always be deleted under Security > Users?
children.body: To actually delete someone, delete the account under Security > Users and the contact under Contacts. That remedy is not always available: after an un-accepted invitation was walked through Edit role, Block, Unblock and Delete, the surviving account could not be deleted under Security > Users - it is absent from POST /api/platform/security/users/search by keyword, by memberId and unfiltered, so the grid cannot show it at all, and DELETE /api/platform/security/users?names= fails with ConcurrencyFailure on every attempt. Control accounts in the same store behave normally; see KB-4A8606CA.
